⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/fixed-read-leaf-seam.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/shared-record-ids.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files. Nothing else in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **2** changed package(s)).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/fixed-read-leaf-seam.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/shared-record-ids.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e343ab7c209c858ee5a7a1fa117baacf96a77229` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d42859d0567775ea9f16cd5ab16fc76afc67a06e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/shared-record-ids.ts + packages/objectql/src/fixed-read-leaf-seam.ts

Inputs read: card #36121 (body and its three comments: triage 7065140496, claim 7099712845, dev report 7103837295), PR #36723 (body, four-file list, net diff against `main`; merge base 3aa008d436, and neither reviewed file nor `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing` changed on `main` since), and the check-runs on this head. Code read in the tree at this head, never reviewed: `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-arm-boot.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/filter-comparand-shape.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/fixed-read-leaf.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts`, ADR-0155's plan, and `sharing-service.ts` as it stood on the parent of #36116's merge commit (52a2398db8) for the sentences about the retired list.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged, right. Every hunk in both `.ts` files sits inside a block comment; no schema, type, export, operator or runtime line moves. `SharedRecordIds`, `isSharedRecordIds`, `SHARED_RECORD_IDS_BRAND`, `driverEvaluatesFixedReadLeaf` and `fixedReadLeafClassOfEngine` keep their signatures.
- Public surface: the published bytes that change are TSDoc only (the module docblock of `@objectstack/spec/data`'s `shared-record-ids.ts`; the module docblock and two symbol docblocks of `@objectstack/objectql`'s seam, one of them on the exported `driverEvaluatesFixedReadLeaf`). No api-surface or export-origins baseline is owed and none is in the diff, right.
- Gate verdicts on this head at read time: `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Check PR Size` and `Flag docs affected by code changes` are completed with success. Still in progress and NOT cited as green: `Build Core`, `Build UI Deps`, `Test Core` (all ten shards), `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Live E2E UI`. This record attests the contract reading only; those runs remain the merge gate's to answer.

### ② Semver level

Two patch changesets, one per touched published package (`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql`): right. The diff publishes changed docblock bytes and nothing else, so patch is the level, and a changeset is owed because the TSDoc ships. Both changeset bodies describe the tree truthfully (plugin-sharing's read and write scopes carry the leaf; plugin-sharing reads `driverEvaluatesFixedReadLeaf` for R2).

Clause-②: no — right. No accept-set narrows or widens; `Metadata-protocol: none` is right for the same reason. The line is on the PR body and on both changesets, and it matches the claim.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report; nothing to answer.
- Dev out-of-scope note, `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-arm-boot.ts:10` ("today's grant read ran that registration"): confirmed in the tree, and confirmed outside this card's surface (the card names the two files and the grep roots `packages/spec/src/data` and `packages/objectql/src`). Leaving it is right for this PR. It is recorded as "noted, not filed"; the adopting seat owes it a carrier (a follow-up card or a fold into the next plugin-sharing prose pass), since no carrier exists today.
- The card's grep, re-read on this head: under the two roots the only grant-list hit was `shared-record-ids.ts:22`, rewritten here. The remaining hits (autonumber seed page size, `MIN_MAX_EXCLUDED_ID_BUDGET`, timeouts, issue numbers, examples) are unrelated, as the dev says.
- Dev deviations (trailer and footer form): process matters for the lane seat, no contract effect.
- SQL push-down: no code changes, so no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The prose now states the push-down that is live (the leaf compiled as a subquery in the list's position; no grant read into memory).

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`packages/spec/src/data/shared-record-ids.ts` — each changed sentence against the tree:

- "It sits where the share arm's list of granted ids sat before the producer's switch (ADR-0155 plan step 6), as the comparand of `$in` on the object's `id`" — true. Before #36116, `buildReadFilter` and `buildWriteFilter` pushed the granted-id list as the `$in` comparand of `id`; on this head `sharing-service.ts:828` and `:948` push `SharedRecordIds.read` / `.write` in that same disjunct position. Plan step 6 in ADR-0155 is "plugin-sharing: the switch".
- "The list the share arm bound before the switch is retired; the share arm now carries this leaf, which is G at every count" — true. `grantedRecordIds` and both `limit: 5000` grant reads are gone from `sharing-service.ts` on this head; no list fallback exists (the seam's own rule). The removed claim, "holds at most 5,000 members of G", was false after the switch. Where R2 applies the producer writes no share arm at all (`shareGrantsInertReason`), which the sentence does not contradict: an arm, where there is one, is the leaf. `contracts/sharing-service.ts` already says the same in the published contract.
- "where the retired list's `recipient_id` came from" — true. The retired reads filtered `recipient_id: context.userId`; the leaf is built from `context.userId` of the same context.
- "The engine's callers of the comparand-shape door admit it (ADR-0155 plan step 2), and that producer writes it from its switch on (plan step 6)" — true. `objectql/src/filter-comparand-shape.ts#assertListComparandShapes` passes `admitFixedReadLeaves: ENGINE_FIXED_READ_LEAF_BRANDS` on every call, and every engine verb reaches the door through it. The only non-test writes of the leaf into a filter are the two plugin-sharing builders; the two other constructions (`share-arm-boot.ts:82`, `sharing-service.ts:1747`) are probes handed to no evaluator, so the unchanged "One producer writes it" still holds. Both removed "until" clauses were false on `main`.
- Sentences kept and still true: "with no cap and no ordering" (① ruled A); the SQL shape; the legality section.

`packages/objectql/src/fixed-read-leaf-seam.ts` — each changed sentence against the tree:

- "the class-② boot check and R2's share-arm answer live with the producer, plugin-sharing (ADR-0155 plan step 6), which is the one writer of the leaf" — true. The boot check is `share-arm-boot.ts#shareGrantRegistrationRefusal`; R2's answer is `SharingService.shareGrantsInertReason`; the seam module still holds neither. `FIXED_READ_LEAF_NAMES` is `['SharedRecordIds']`, so "the leaf" has one writer.
- "The one reader of the declaration: the seam's consult, and the producer's up-front answer (R2, ADR-0155 plan step 6), which reaches the driver through `IDataEngine.getDriverForObject`" — true. `supports.fixedReadLeaves` is read only inside `driverEvaluatesFixedReadLeaf`, called at the seam (`passFixedReadLeaves`) and at `sharing-service.ts:1763`, where the driver comes from `this.engine.getDriverForObject(object)`; `IDataEngine` declares that member. Drivers declare the list; none reads it.
- "which the retired list's read of the table ran and the subquery would read around" — true. The retired list was read with `engine.find('sys_record_share', …)`, so object-scoped middleware and find hooks registered for the table by name ran on it; the subquery is evaluated inside the driver and passes neither. The code's own refusal text states the general form ("which a read of the table runs").
- Kept and still true: line 5's "`SharedRecordIds` today"; "At this step both answer with the refusal (R1)" (`passFixedReadLeaves` throws for both classes).

Tried to break it: looked for a surviving list path or cap in the share arm (none), a second writer of the leaf (none outside probes and testkits), a second reader of the declaration (none), an engine door call that does not admit the leaf (none), and stale future or present tense left in either file (`today`, `until`, `lands`, `yet`: only seam line 5, which is true).

- N1 (nit) — the spec sentence names only the engine's callers as admitting the leaf; the analytics read-scope door also admits it (`READ_SCOPE_FIXED_READ_LEAF_BRANDS`, plan step 5). The sentence is true as written and was engine-only before this diff; accepted as it stands, no change asked.
